content.title: What to do and What not to do: messages from the Guidelines
content.summary: Healthcare providers and policymakers should be conscious of potential gender bias in the management of ACS and ensure women with ACS receive evidence-based care. Patient recruitment to RCTs should reflect real-world populations from different socioeconomic backgrounds. Several studies report a disproportionately low proportion of women recruited to cardiovascular trials, alongside historic under-representation of older patients and ethnic minorities, suggesting an underlying recruitment bias. Increased representation of female patients in future clinical trials is required to better inform optimal management of women with ACS.
key_points: Be aware of potential gender bias in ACS management and ensure evidence-based care for women.
Ensure patient recruitment in RCTs reflects real-world, socioeconomically diverse populations.
Recognize and address under-representation of women, older patients, and ethnic minorities in cardiovascular trials.
Increase representation of female patients in future clinical trials to improve management guidance.
